design_rationale:
WORKLOG — car_rental_desk task 0 (drive / Car Rental Rate Classes)

STEP 0 — draw, asset ledger and claim.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/tasks/car_rental_desk --tasks 2 printed:
  task 0: prerequisite_problems=1, problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 5]
  task 1: prerequisite_problems=1, problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 6]
So this task's tree is exactly two problems (one prerequisite), and each of its two computations
declares exactly five factors. drive_ext_additional_driver_charge took 5 and drive_ext_release_charge
took 5. Nothing about the tree or the factor sets was chosen by hand.

Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is the first). Claimed here: base subjects
drive_extras_charge (through drive_ext_additional_driver_charge) and drive_cancellation_charge
(through drive_ext_release_charge), with the task tools charge_additional_driver_79b211ed and
release_rental_booking_4b632ce9. Left free for task 1: drive_mileage_grant, drive_return,
drive_mileage_use, drive_fuel_charge, drive_damage_charge, drive_refund_payout, drive_rate_charge,
drive_no_show_charge, drive_driver_amend and drive_supplier_notice — task 1 takes the collection
allowance and the return settlement, which is an independent, load-bearing space with its own
prerequisite edge and its own owner=user write.

Why it is a good test. The caller asks one thing — what it costs to give a car hire up — and the
number she is owed cannot be reached from the rate class alone. The desk must (a) reconcile the rental's
own ledger line by line, telling the money the release share acts on from the lines it must leave
out and from the neighbouring rental's lines entirely; (b) discover
from the release policy's own wording that the charge is fixed only once the ledger carries the
additional driver charge owed for the drivers named on the agreement, find that no such line stands,
and raise it first; (c) price that driver charge itself from four live conditions (club standing,
the length of the agreement, the waiver standing on it, how far ahead it was booked) and a
weighting rule; and (d) then take the release share against the right slice of the ledger, take the
uncollected equipment back out of it, and apply two reliefs in the order the policy states. No step
is a tool choice: both tools are hidden, atomic and blind to the policy.

STEP 0 cards.
Base-invariant card — write 1 (drive_extras_charge, additional driver line):
  drive_rate_and_extras / rental_open_for_extras, kind=state, condition "An optional item is sold
  only while the rental record stands at confirmed or picked up." Authority system_record,
  pre_action, correlation drive_rentals.drive_rental_id -> the call's drive_rental_id.
  Satisfied: initial_state.drive_rentals.12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82.status = "confirmed" at frozen_time, and the same row
  is the object the call names. Negative case: had the rental stood at cancelled or no_show the item
  could not be sold at all, and the correct terminal state would be to refuse the line.
  drive_club_and_corporate_interaction governs the same subject and carries no structured gate, so
  it enters as policy_scope: it fixes that the club tier decides what the rental is charged and that
  a corporate programme reference would replace consumer pricing; this rental carries
  corporate_program_id = "" so consumer pricing stands.
Base-invariant card — write 2 (drive_cancellation_charge, release line):
  drive_cancellation governs the subject and its only structured gate, inside_free_cancellation, is
  declared applies_to drive_cancel, not to the charge line, so the charge write inherits the policy
  as policy_scope. The free-cancellation term itself is still live law and is the reason a charge
  arises at all: the class booked is the Pay At Counter Flex Rate, whose free-cancellation term runs
  24 elapsed hours from the supplier's confirmation
  (initial_state.drive_rentals.12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82.confirmed_at = 2026-09-08 16:41:00 CDT). frozen_time is
  2026-09-17 11:20:00 CDT, some nine days later, so the term has long run out and the release is
  charged rather than free. Boundary: a release confirmed at 2026-09-09 16:41:00 CDT would have been
  exactly at the boundary and still free; one at 16:42 would not.
Business-object card: the narrowest object is the rental whose agreement number is RA7K42QP9,
  initial_state.drive_rentals.12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82. Every aggregate in both computations is scoped to that rental id
  by the ledger primitives themselves. The renter's earlier, closed rental
  initial_state.drive_rentals.1f698a91-48bc-4f71-a8be-fb21f58a1dba carries its own prepayment, four rental-day lines, an agency
  service fee and an additional driver line; none of them may enter either sum, and none can, because
  they carry a different drive_rental_id. Both task tools write the rental id they are given into the
  new line, so the derived rows stay correlated to their source object.
Problem-tree card:
  root problem  drive_ext_release_charge (what the caller asks about)
  prerequisite  drive_ext_additional_driver_charge
  edge          drive_ext_release_charge <- drive_ext_additional_driver_charge
                kind value_input; gate = the compute binding chargeable_base; form state
                prerequisite sentence (verbatim in the release policy's own rule): "The release
                charge is fixed only after the rental's ledger carries the additional driver charge
                owed for the drivers named on the agreement."
                four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after"; (2) the side waited on
                is a record-visible state — a kind of entry standing on the rental's ledger — and
                names no action and no performer; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id and no
                code token; (4) it is a hard requirement ("only after") over exactly the item kind
                the edge's condition names, no wider and no narrower.
                exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the additional driver
                line is booked by drive_ext_additional_driver_charge and by nothing else in the
                charter, so the reader who sees the state missing has one and only one problem to
                resolve. Derivation: the sentence says the release charge waits on an additional
                driver line standing on the ledger; the ledger (48 seeded lines) carries a waiver,
                satellite navigation, child seat, licence fee and agency fee but no additional driver
                line; the additional driver policy's own rule says what an additional driver charge
                is and that it is owed for every driver named beyond the free count; therefore the
                additional driver charge must be raised first.
                condition: the rental's ledger carries a line for the additional driver charge owed
                for the drivers named on the agreement.
                resolved by charge_additional_driver_79b211ed, owner=agent.
                unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.drive_rental_entries holds no row for
                rental 12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82 with charge_category additional_driver, while
                initial_state.drive_rentals.12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82.additional_drivers_count = 4 and the class carries
                one driver free, so a charge is genuinely owed and genuinely absent.
  topological order: drive_ext_additional_driver_charge, then drive_ext_release_charge.
  parallel edges: none (a single edge), so the order is forced and no commutation argument is needed.
  deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the additional driver write leaves the release charge
  at 77.11 instead of 103.37 — the edge carries 26.26 of the scored number.
  owner=user problem: the root. Giving up a confirmed rental is the renter's own act on her own
  booking (drive_cancellation: "Only the renter may cancel their own confirmed rental, and the
  cancellation is confirmed by the renter rather than performed on their behalf."), so
  release_rental_booking_4b632ce9 is owner=user, unlocked and handed over by the agent at the root's
  place in the order and run by the caller herself.

STEP 1 — policies. Two extended policies, both layered on base and both declaring their overrides.
  drive_ext_additional_driver_charge overrides one clause of drive_rate_and_extras (the flat
  "per driver per rental day" sentence) because it prices the same quantity differently in the same
  world: base would give 4 drivers x 10 days x 12.00 = 480.00 before the class's free driver is
  taken off, the extended rule gives 102.96. Everything else in drive_rate_and_extras — the state
  gate, the inclusion rules for protection products, the sales-tax ordering — is inherited untouched.
  drive_ext_release_charge overrides one clause of drive_cancellation (the sentence reading the
  charge off the rate class's ladder) and replaces it with its own notice-share ladder; the free
  cancellation clauses, the supplier-fault clause and the after-collection clause are inherited.
  Trigger types: the driver charge is state_due — with nobody calling at all, a rental carrying four
  named drivers owes that line at month-end reconciliation; the release charge is on_request — it
  arises only because this caller asks to give the hire up.
  Rule / compute two-way sweep. Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses quotes its
  rule sentence verbatim in compute_basis (club_tier, club_qualifying_12m, free_driver_count,
  booked_days, charged_days, cdw_days, fee_per_day, advance_days, advance_relief_pct,
  driver_weight_total, result; and on the release side ledger_collected, agency_fee_total,
  prepayment_total, rate_line_total, chargeable_base, days_to_collection, withheld_share_pct,
  equipment_total, returned_items_total, air_status, air_refund_form, disruption_relief_pct,
  club_tier_a, club_years, member_relief_pct, result). Reverse: every load-bearing sentence of each
  rule is claimed by a binding — the twelve-month window by within_months=12 on the club ledger read,
  "for every booked rental day" by the DAYS span, "a collision damage waiver line stands for every
  booked rental day" by the COUNT filter, "the agency service fee left out of it" by the
  charge_category filter, the two reliefs "one after the other" by the two successive factors in
  result, and "rounded to two decimal places only at the end" by the single RND at the end of each
  compute. Ordering and grouping are written out in prose in both rules rather than left to a
  summary word, and neither rule restates the other's prerequisite sentence.

STEP 3 — the world, and why each class of row is load-bearing.
  customers.a5d0081a-03e1-477c-b4a2-771821c68e27: the caller. Mobile 6302884157 and passport_last4 1673 sit in this difficulty's
  identifier band (6302xxxxxx, 1600-1799).
  drive_rentals.12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82: the object of the call. status confirmed (satisfies the extras gate, and is
  why a release is possible at all); variant Pay At Counter Flex Rate (free count 1, driver fee
  12.00, flat cancellation charge 50.00); additional_drivers_count 4 (remove it and the driver charge
  is nil and the edge lapses); rental_days 10 with pickup 2026-09-27 and dropoff 2026-10-07 (the
  seven-to-thirteen day tier of the charged-day basis; make it 6 and that factor falls to its
  fall-through); booked_date 2026-09-06 against pickup 2026-09-27 is exactly 21 days, the inclusive
  boundary of the early naming tier; vehicle_class suv, which is deliberately NOT one of the
  premium, luxury or van classes, so the waiver-backed fee lands on the second tier and not the
  first; corporate_program_id empty, so consumer pricing and the naming relief both stand.
  charges_total_usd is seeded at 562.15, exactly the sum of the rental's own ledger lines, which is
  the identity the schema declares for that field; the same holds of the closed rental (501.95) and
  of both rentals' mileage allowances. No compute reads any of them — every money figure in this task
  is taken from the ledger rows themselves — so the fields corroborate the ledger rather than
  offering a second answer beside it. The confirmed_at of 2026-09-08 16:41:00 CDT is the free-cancellation anchor.
  drive_rental_entries: 41 lines on 12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82 — one agency service fee, ten waiver days, ten satellite
  navigation days, ten child seat days and ten licence fee days. The ten waiver lines are what put
  cdw_days at 10 and so at or above the ten booked days; the satellite navigation and child seat
  lines are the equipment the release returns; the licence fee lines are statutory and are NOT
  equipment, which is the near miss a careless reader folds into the return; the agency fee line is
  the one the release share must leave out. Seven further lines belong to the closed rental 1f698a91-48bc-4f71-a8be-fb21f58a1dba
  and are excluded by their rental id alone.
  club_memberships.429792c1-d19c-4f02-b162-163d3155e324: Wanderlane Gold, active, enrolled 2019-04-12 — the tier that takes the
  middle free-driver tier and, with more than two years held, the high membership relief; its tier took effect at the annual review of
  2025-08-31, which is the clear-down row's own date, so the qualifying figure the row carries is the
  sum over the current qualifying period as well as the sum of every qualifying movement seeded.
  club_points_entries: three qualifying accruals inside the last twelve months (3200 + 2100 + 1500 =
  6800, at or above the 6000 middle threshold) plus the annual qualifying clear-down of -1100 posted
  2025-08-31, which is twelve whole months back and therefore outside the window — the near miss, and
  a biting one: a reader who folds it in gets 5700, below the 6000 threshold, and drops to the
  fall-through tier and a different scored number. The membership row's own qualifying figure is
  exactly that 5700, being the sum of every qualifying movement seeded on the ledger as the schema
  declares, so the field and the rule's twelve-month window now part company: reading the field off
  the holding gives the wrong tier, and only the windowed ledger read gives the right one. A
  spendable accrual of 18400 and a redemption of -9000 are not qualifying points at all, and the
  membership's spendable balance is the 9400 they sum to.
  air_bookings.87787a73-bd0c-4f69-aa4f-a22921d0a615: the Denver flights, cancelled, value returned as travel_credit — the tier of
  the disruption relief. Without this row the relief is nil and the release charge is 172.28.
  Automatic-clause check: nothing seeded lights a base automatic clause this task set cannot carry.
  The rental is confirmed and uncollected, so no rental day, mileage grant, fuel settlement or
  damage recharge is yet owed on it; the closed rental is settled and archived; the club rows carry
  no expiry due before frozen_time.

STEP 4 — persona. Marisol volunteers only the surface goal (she wants to give the hire up and wants
  to know the cost first), the natural circumstances (the trip fell through) and the hard preference
  that she confirm it herself. Identity, the record locator, the club card and the flight
  cancellation come out only when asked. The additional driver charge is never mentioned, hinted at
  or asked after: her only contribution to it is the passive branch in which, after the agent has
  explained that something must go onto the booking first, she says to go ahead without asking what
  it is. Her last reaction answers the last gold action — the release — and stops there; she asks
  for no document, no statement and no further work.

STEP 5 — verification. Run:
  .venv/bin/python scratch/t0_calc.py   (the harness reproduced in the gates)
  B (drive_ext_additional_driver_charge), evaluated on the opening world:
    club_tier = Wanderlane Gold; club_qualifying_12m = 6800 -> free_driver_count = 2
    chargeable_drivers = max(0, 4 - 2) = 2
    booked_days = 10 -> charged_days = 7 + (10-7) x 0.5 = 8.5
    cdw_days = 10 >= 10 and vehicle_class = suv -> fee_per_day = 9.50
    advance_days = 21 -> advance_relief_pct = 15
    driver_weight_total = 1 + (2-1) x 0.5 = 1.5
    result = RND(1.5 x 8.5 x 9.50 x 0.85, 2) = 102.96
    factor sensitivity: club_free_driver_allowance 137.28, charged_day_length_basis 121.12,
      waiver_backed_driver_fee 130.05, advance_naming_relief 121.12, multi_driver_weighting 137.28;
      whole baseline 360.00. Every one differs from 102.96.
  A (drive_ext_release_charge), evaluated after B's write has landed:
    ledger_collected = 562.15 + 102.96 = 665.11; agency_fee_total = 9.95; prepayment_total = 0;
    rate_line_total = 0 -> chargeable_base = 655.16
    days_to_collection = DAYS(2026-09-17, 2026-09-27) = 10 -> withheld_share_pct = 50
    equipment_total = 119.90 + 129.90 = 249.80, given up 10 days ahead -> returned in full
    air_status = cancelled, air_refund_form = travel_credit -> disruption_relief_pct = 40
    club_tier_a = Wanderlane Gold, club_years = 7.4 -> member_relief_pct = 15
    result = RND(0.5 x (655.16 - 249.80) x 0.60 x 0.85, 2) = 103.37
    factor sensitivity: notice_band_share 206.73, withheld_money_basis 105.90,
      linked_disruption_relief 172.28, membership_release_relief 121.61,
      uncollected_equipment_return 167.07; whole baseline 665.11. Every one differs from 103.37.
  Prerequisite sensitivity: replaying everything except the additional driver write gives
    ledger_collected 562.15, chargeable_base 552.20 and a release charge of 77.11 rather than
    103.37, so the edge carries the scored number and is not decorative.
  Handling time: B is evaluated on the opening world because it has no prerequisite; A is evaluated
    on the opening world plus B's line, never on the opening world alone.

STEP 6 — evaluation. Reads locate and verify first, then pull the rentals, the rental's own ledger,
  the club membership, the club points ledger and the air booking — every row any factor's tier rests
  on. The ledger read is also the read that shows the additional driver line missing, which is how
  the prerequisite is discoverable at all. Writes run in the tree's topological order: the additional
  driver line (agent, through unlock then call) and then the release (unlocked by the agent and run
  by the caller herself through call_user_discoverable_tool). Neither tool checks the other: the
  release tool posts whatever amount it is given whether or not a driver line stands, so the
  consequence of missing the prerequisite shows up only in the terminal hash.

Draft recomputation from the visible context alone (extended yaml, compute, expected, GT and this
  dossier masked): reading only what the published terms will say, the tool schemas, the rows the
  share tools return and what Marisol actually says, an agent reaches: the hire may be given up; the
  object is the rental with agreement number RA7K42QP9; the release charge waits on an additional
  driver line that is not there; that line prices at 102.96 on the Gold free-driver tier, the
  seven-to-thirteen day charged-day basis, the waivered fee and the twenty-one day naming relief;
  the release then takes half of the ledger less the agency fee and less the equipment returned, and
  two successive reliefs, giving 103.37. Same object, same order, same two numbers as gold.

Revisions: none since first write; the seed was authored to the drawn counts and the factor
  sensitivity run passed on its first execution.


MANUAL VALUES GATES (run after the per-task scripts passed; results recorded here).
 Length and breadth: surface goal "give the hire up, what does it cost" -> the release policy's own
   prerequisite sentence -> the missing additional driver line -> that line priced from the club
   free-driver tier, the charged-day basis, the waiver-backed fee, the naming relief and the
   multi-driver weighting -> the release share against the right slice of the ledger, less the
   equipment returned, relieved twice. Removing any load-bearing dependency moves a number: the
   edge moves the release by 26.26, and each of the ten factors moves its own result (figures in
   Step 5). One problem of the tree, the root, is resolved by an owner=user tool, and giving up a
   confirmed rental genuinely requires the renter in person under drive_cancellation; it completes
   on the spot.
 Need and simulator boundary: the caller states the object (the Denver hire), the timing (now,
   before anything is done), the authorisation (the desk may act first; she confirms the release
   herself) and that this is a write, not a quote only. She never reads policy, never corrects a
   figure and never runs the release tool until the agent hands it over.
 Opening-world chronology: every fact she volunteers points at a seeded row — the flights cancelled
   two days before frozen_time (air_bookings.cancelled_at 2026-09-15), the membership since 2019
   (enrolled_date 2019-04-12), ten days from the twenty-seventh (rental_days 10, pickup 2026-09-27),
   an SUV (vehicle_class suv), booked the same day as the flights (both booked_date 2026-09-06), and
   a run of small charges the day the supplier came back (all lines posted 2026-09-08, the
   confirmation date). Nothing she says foresees a figure gold produces.
 Base eligibility and time anchors: rental_open_for_extras satisfied at frozen_time on status
   "confirmed"; the free-cancellation term of the Pay At Counter Flex Rate is 24 elapsed hours from
   confirmed_at 2026-09-08 16:41, so 2026-09-09 16:41 would still be free and frozen_time
   2026-09-17 11:20 is far outside it — which is why a charge is due at all.
 Authoritative facts and the business object: status, the ledger and the club and air records are
   all system records; the persona claims none of them as settled fact. Every aggregate is scoped to
   rental RA7K42QP9, and the closed November rental's seven lines are excluded by their own rental
   reference.
 Reachability with no real-world wait: locate, verify, four reads, then two writes, all under one
   frozen_time. Nothing waits on a payment clearing, a supplier reply or a future date.
 Prerequisite sentence: four-point test recorded above; the state form was available and used; the
   rule carries nothing else about the dependency and names no tool.
 Factors bear weight and the labels are honest: each factor's baseline is exactly what the baseline
   paragraph states (the class's free driver count, every booked day, the class's own driver fee, no
   relief, each driver counted alike; and for the release the whole ledger at the standard share with
   nothing returned and no relief). The two method factors change how a quantity is computed (the
   days charged for, the money the share acts on) rather than swapping a number. No two tiers of any
   ladder select the same outcome.
 Draft recomputation from the visible context: performed and recorded in Step 5; it agrees with gold
   on the object, the order and both numbers.


REWORK ROUND 2 — closing the source-layer audit of revision_4
(env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/car_rental_desk/_difficulty.md and 0.md). Every item the
report raises against this task is answered here; the scored values 102.96 and 103.37 are unchanged and
were re-verified after every change.

T0-3 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (the stamp on qualifying_points_pts). CLOSED.
  symptom: the membership row carried 6800, exactly the figure club_free_driver_allowance's ladder asks
    the reader to compute with the twelve-month window, so reading the field and reading the ledger could
    not be told apart by the score, and the computation's only near-miss was neutralised with it.
  root cause: the summary field had been set to the rule's rolling-twelve-month aggregate instead of to
    the quantity the schema defines for it.
  change: the out-of-window qualifying row is now the annual qualifying clear-down of -1100 posted
    2025-08-31 (event type club_qualifying_reset, reason annual_reset) rather than a +4900 accrual, and
    the membership carries qualifying_points_pts = 5700 — the exact sum of every qualifying movement
    seeded, which is what the schema declares, and also the sum over the current qualifying period, the
    tier having taken effect at that same annual review on 2025-08-31. points_balance_pts is likewise
    the 9400 the spendable rows sum to.
  result: the field and the rule now part company in the score. The rule's window gives 6800 and the
    middle tier (two drivers free, 102.96); the field gives 5700, below the 6000 threshold, and the
    fall-through tier (the class's one free driver, 137.28). An agent that reads the stamp instead of
    the windowed ledger now books a different number, and the near-miss bites for the first time: folding
    the out-of-window clear-down into the sum produces the same wrong 5700. The scored value is
    unchanged because the three in-window accruals are unchanged; check_compute re-run green.

T0-1 / D-1 — the holding total against the ledger. CLOSED.
  symptom: charges_total_usd stood at 432.25 while the rental's ledger summed to 562.15, and the schema
    declares the two identically equal, so "the money standing on the rental's ledger" had two readings
    and the second gave 70.24 instead of 103.37.
  root cause: a stale cache was deliberately seeded against a schema that words the relation as an
    identity rather than as a figure that may lag.
  change: charges_total_usd is now the exact ledger sum on both seeded rentals (562.15 and 501.95), and
    mileage_allowance_remaining is the exact sum of each rental's mileage movements — the closed rental
    now carries the grant of 700 miles its four days at the class's 175 a day earned and the 486 it drove
    off, which is exactly the 214 its allowance field shows. The persona no longer sets a remembered
    figure against the account: she says she has not been keeping track and asks the desk to go by the
    account itself.
  result: one figure for the money on the ledger, on every rental of this world. The alternative 70.24
    has no ground left. No compute reads any summary field, so no scored value moves; replay, solvability
    and compute re-run green.

T0-2 — the closure's evidence for why the prerequisite is unmet. CLOSED.
  symptom: unresolved_at_frozen_time.evidence listed charges_total_usd, which shows nothing about whether
    an additional driver line stands on the ledger.
  change: the evidence now cites the agreement's additional_drivers_count, its rate class, and one of the
    ledger lines that does stand (a collision damage waiver day), and why_false names the five line kinds
    the ledger actually carries and the one it does not.
  result: the closure's evidence and its prose now rest on the same fact. Figures unchanged (552.20 ->
    655.16; 103.37 against 77.11).

T0-4 / D-2 — the free-cancellation gloss. MITIGATED inside this difficulty's own write domain.
  The parameter_schema gloss ("Hours before collection by which a cancellation carries no charge") is a
  base-layer defect and base is frozen, so it is not touched here; the coordinator has it recorded as a
  known issue. What this round restores is the mitigation an earlier round relied on: drive_ext_release_charge's
  own rule now states the anchor outright — "The free-cancellation term this scope refers to runs forward
  from the moment the supplier confirmed the renter's booking, and never backwards from the scheduled
  collection moment." — so the extended rule that consumes the term names the confirmation anchor and
  rejects the backwards-from-collection reading in its own words, and the KB will carry that sentence
  beside the gloss. On this world the term ran out on 2026-09-09 16:41 CDT, eight days before the call.

D-6 — "before this call" in the tool docstrings. CLOSED. Every Args entry now reads "as it stands on the
  rental record returned by the car rental lookup", and the one remaining ordering word in the module is
  a formatting note ("no unit written after it"). The Id-class contract still names where the reference is
  reachable. TASK TOOL CONTRACT re-run green.

D-7 — base's drive_mileage orders the grant before the return. ACCEPTED as an observation. The sentence is
  base and base is frozen; no edge of this difficulty rests on it (both edges are grounded in the blocked
  policy's own prerequisite sentence), which is the ground on which the report itself records it as an
  observation rather than a red.

Summary fields after this task's own writes. Every summary field satisfies the identity the schema
declares on the seeded world. The two gold writes then add ledger rows without touching the holding's
cached total, as every task tool in this framework does — a tool may not aggregate a history into a
derived value — so at the release's handling time the cached total lags the rows by exactly the
additional driver line the agent has just raised. Nothing turns on it: the release rule says "the money
standing on the rental's ledger", the ledger being this category's event table, and the prerequisite
sentence has already sent the reader to the very line that makes the two differ.
user_scenario:
Marisol Okonkwo-Reyes is forty-two, runs a small design studio in Chicago's West Town, and is ringing from the studio between meetings with a mug of coffee going cold beside her. She is brisk and a little rueful rather than cross: the Denver trip she had built around a long weekend of hiking with her sister's family has fallen through, and she is working through the pieces of it one call at a time.

She opens by saying the car she has booked in Denver for the end of the month is no longer any use to her and she wants to give it up, and that she would like to know what giving it up is going to cost her before anything is done to the booking. If the agent asks how to find her she gives the mobile number the booking notifications go to, 6302884157, reading it out digit by digit. Asked for something more to prove who she is she offers her date of birth, 1984-02-11, and if that is not enough on its own she reads out the last four characters of the passport held on file, 1673. None of that comes out unprompted, and she will not read a card number to anybody over the telephone.

The booking reference is somewhere in her email but she cannot put her hand on it while she is talking; if she is asked for it she says she will have to go digging and asks whether the mobile number will do instead. She does know the hire was for ten days from the twenty-seventh, that it is an SUV, and that she booked it the same day as the flights, and she says so if any of it is asked. She is vague about what has actually gone onto her card so far: she remembers a run of small charges landing the day the supplier came back to her, and if the agent reads her a total she says mildly that she has not been keeping track of it herself and asks them to go by whatever the account itself says.

If she is asked whether anything else about the trip has changed she says the flights have already gone: she cancelled the Denver flights two days ago and the money is sitting with Wanderlane as credit rather than back on her card. She gives the record locator QH7TZB if it is asked for. Her Wanderlane card comes up only if she is asked whether she is a member, and then she says she has been with the programme since 2019 and thinks she is on the gold tier now; she has no idea how many points are on it and says so.

She will not push the desk toward anything it has not offered. When the agent explains that something has to be put onto the booking before the cost of giving it up can be worked out, she says that is fine, go ahead, and waits without asking what it is. When she is told what giving the hire up will cost and is asked to confirm it herself, she says yes, she understands, and she does it in person rather than having the agent do it for her, using whatever the agent hands her. Once she hears that the hire has been released and the charge recorded against it, she thanks them, says that is one more thing off the list, and rings off.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: No money may be moved on the account until this has passed; both the driver line and the release are money movements.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the car rentals standing in the caller's name, and pick out the confirmed Denver hire she is asking about.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Supplies the rate class, the status, the booked days, the collection and return moments, the booked date, the vehicle class, the named additional drivers and the corporate reference that every tier of both computations rests on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every line posted to the caller's car rentals in one pass, then keep only those carrying the Denver rental's own reference: its agency service fee, its waiver days, its satellite navigation and child seat days and its licence fee days.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Gives the money the release share acts on, the waiver day count behind the per-day driver fee and the equipment total the release returns, shows that no additional driver line stands on that rental yet, and makes plain that the closed November rental's own prepayment, rate and driver lines belong to a different agreement and enter none of the sums.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier decides how many additional drivers the agreement carries free, and the tier together with how long the membership has been held decides the membership relief on the release charge.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the membership's points ledger and total the qualifying points accrued over the last twelve months.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The qualifying total is the second condition of the free-driver tier; the accrual that fell outside the twelve months must be left out of it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the air booking the trip was built around, its status and the form its value came back in.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Whether that booking stands cancelled or refunded, and whether the value came back as a travel credit or to the card, decides the disruption relief on the release charge.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the additional driver charge owed for the drivers named on the Denver hire, so that the rental's ledger carries the line the release charge waits on.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: drive_ext_additional_driver_charge is the only policy that computes an additional driver charge, and its result is this call's additional_driver_charge_usd.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.drive_rental_id: The confirmed Denver hire, agreement number RA7K42QP9. Basis: the car rental lookup at action 2 returns exactly one rental of the caller's standing at confirmed for collection on 2026-09-27, and the tool's own schema says the reference is 'the reference number of the car rental agreement the charge belongs to; read it from the rental record returned by the car rental lookup before this call'. Uniqueness: the caller's only other rental is closed, was collected in November 2025 and returned to ORDA3, so it answers neither the agreement she describes nor the state an optional item may be sold in; any correct agent lands on the same rental.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.additional_driver_charge_usd: 102.96. The agreement names four additional drivers; the traveller club membership is active at Wanderlane Gold with 6800 qualifying points accrued inside the last twelve months (3200 on 2026-01-19, 2100 on 2026-04-26 and 1500 on 2026-07-14; the qualifying clear-down of -1100 posted 2025-08-31 falls outside the window, and the 5700 the membership row itself shows is that clear-down folded in and would put her on no free-driver tier at all), which carries two drivers free, leaving two chargeable. The agreement books ten days from 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-07, so the days charged are seven in full plus half a day for each of the three further days, that is 8.5. A collision damage waiver line stands for each of the ten booked days and the vehicle booked is an SUV rather than a premium, luxury or van class, so the waivered driver fee of 9.50 applies for each chargeable day. The agreement was booked on 2026-09-06, twenty-one days before collection, and carries no corporate programme reference, so the early naming relief of 15 percent applies. Two chargeable drivers on an agreement of seven or more days are weighted as one whole driver plus half of the second, that is 1.5. 1.5 x 8.5 x 9.50 = 121.125, relieved once by 15 percent, gives 102.95625, rounded to 102.96. Any agent who reads the same rows and applies the same rule converges on it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the renter's own release tool and hand it to the caller, who gives up the rental herself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Giving up a confirmed rental is the renter's own act on her own booking, so the tool is hers to run; the unlock changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The caller gives the Denver hire up herself: the rental is recorded as cancelled and the release charge is withheld on its ledger.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: drive_ext_release_charge is the only policy that computes a release charge, and its result is this call's release_charge_usd; the caller performs the write because the rental is hers to give up.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.drive_rental_id: The same confirmed Denver hire, agreement number RA7K42QP9. Basis: the car rental lookup at action 2 returns it as the caller's only rental standing at confirmed, and the tool's schema says the reference is 'the reference number of the renter's own car rental agreement being given up; read it from the rental record returned by the car rental lookup before this call'. Uniqueness: the closed November rental cannot be given up and is not the hire she describes, so no second rental answers the request.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.release_charge_usd: 103.37. After the additional driver line of 102.96 is raised, the rental's ledger stands at 665.11 (9.95 agency service fee, 259.90 of waiver days, 119.90 of satellite navigation, 129.90 of child seat, 42.50 of licence fee and the 102.96 driver line). The ledger carries no prepayment and no rental day has been priced, so the share acts on the ledger with the agency service fee left out: 655.16. Ten whole days lie between 2026-09-17 and the collection day of 2026-09-27, which is the three-to-thirteen day band and a share of 50 percent. The rental is given up more than three days ahead, so the satellite navigation and child seat lines, 249.80 together, are returned in full and taken out first, leaving 405.36; the licence fee is statutory and is not equipment. Half of that is 202.68. The caller's air booking stands cancelled with its value returned as a travel credit, so the disruption relief of 40 percent applies, leaving 121.608; her active Wanderlane Gold membership, held since 2019-04-12 and so well past two years, then relieves 15 percent of what is left, giving 103.3668, rounded to 103.37. The two reliefs act one after the other and are never added into one rate.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The additional driver write lands one line of 102.96 US dollars with charge_category additional_driver on that rental's ledger, so the state holds and the money the release share acts on rises from 552.20 to 655.16.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has one edge and therefore one legal order: the additional driver line, then the release. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder, and the release write is the last write of the task, so no commutation argument arises.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the additional driver write and replaying everything else leaves the rental's ledger at 562.15 and the money the share acts on at 552.20, so the release charge computes as 77.11 instead of 103.37 — the scored release parameter moves by 26.26.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions an additional driver, a driver fee, or anything owed on the booking. Marisol names only the hire, the wish to give it up and the wish to know the cost first; she never asks whether something must be sorted out first and never hints that anything is outstanding. Her only contribution to the prerequisite is the passive branch in which, after the agent has explained that something must go onto the booking before the cost can be worked out, she says to go ahead — and even there she does not ask what it is.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: release_rental_booking_4b632ce9 in task_tools.py reads the rental row only to copy the customer reference onto the new line, then creates the release line and updates the rental's status; it never looks for an additional driver line, never raises an error and never hints. charge_additional_driver_79b211ed likewise creates its line unconditionally. Calling the release first would succeed and simply write a different, wrong amount.

factor_trace: club_free_driver_allowance (parameter): the membership row is active at Wanderlane Gold and the points ledger carries 3200 + 2100 + 1500 = 6800 qualifying points inside the last twelve months (the qualifying clear-down of -1100 posted 2025-08-31 falls outside it, and the membership row's own qualifying figure of 5700 is that clear-down folded in), so the middle tier applies and two drivers are carried free; the baseline, the free count the rate class itself states, is one.

charged_day_length_basis (method): pickup 2026-09-27 to dropoff 2026-10-07 is ten booked days, so the seven-to-thirteen day tier applies and the days charged are seven in full plus half a day for each of the three further days, 8.5; the baseline, every booked rental day, would give 10.

waiver_backed_driver_fee (parameter): ten collision damage waiver lines stand against ten booked days and the vehicle booked is an SUV, so the waivered driver fee of 9.50 applies; the baseline, the rate class's own additional driver fee, is 12.00.

advance_naming_relief (parameter): booked_date 2026-09-06 is exactly twenty-one days before the 2026-09-27 collection and the agreement carries no corporate programme reference, so the early naming relief of 15 percent applies; the baseline relieves nothing.

multi_driver_weighting (method): two drivers are chargeable on an agreement of ten days, so the first is taken whole and the second at half, giving 1.5; the baseline, each chargeable driver taken whole, would give 2.

bindings belonging to no factor: chargeable_drivers = max(0, 4 - 2) = 2 is the plain subtraction the rule states, and result multiplies the weighted drivers by the days charged and the per-day fee before applying the relief once and rounding at the end.

factor_trace: notice_band_share (parameter): ten whole days lie between 2026-09-17 and the 2026-09-27 collection day, which is the three-to-thirteen day band, so the near notice share of 50 percent applies; the baseline, the standard release share, withholds 100 percent.

withheld_money_basis (method): the ledger carries no prepayment line and no rental day has been priced, so the share acts on the ledger with the agency service fee of 9.95 left out, 655.16; the baseline acts on the whole ledger, 665.11.
linked_disruption_relief (parameter): the caller's air booking stands cancelled with refund_form travel_credit, so the credit disruption relief of 40 percent applies; the baseline relieves nothing.

membership_release_relief (parameter): the membership is active at Wanderlane Gold and was enrolled on 2019-04-12, well past the two-year membership relief term, so the high membership relief of 15 percent applies; the baseline relieves nothing.

uncollected_equipment_return (method): satellite navigation and child seat lines totalling 249.80 stand on the ledger and the rental is given up ten whole days before collection, so every equipment line is returned in full and taken out before the share; the baseline returns nothing. The licence fee lines are statutory and are not equipment.

bindings belonging to no factor: ledger_collected sums the rental's own lines including the 102.96 raised at the previous write, and result applies the share once and then the two reliefs one after the other, rounding only at the end.
